item.title: Library To Celebrate Noon Year’s Eve At Both Branches
item.description: Courtesy/Los Alamos County COUNTY News: Both branches of the Los Alamos Public Library invite families to ring in the new year early with the annual Noon Year’s Eve celebration Wednesday, Dec. 31. The free program runs from 10:30 a.m. to 12:15 p.m. The annual Noon Year’s Eve celebration offers families with younger children a chance to celebrate at a kid-friendly hour. item.title: Española Humane Offers Fee-Waived Puppy Adoptions
item.description: EH News: ESPANOLA, N.M. — Española Humane is offering fee-waived puppy adoptions from Dec. 29 through Jan. 4, helping young dogs find homes while the shelter continues recovery work following recent roof repairs. The shelter is also welcoming guided walk-throughs of the dog kennels with a staff escort, allowing visitors to safely meet adoptable dogs during ongoing mold remediation. item.title: Local Love Holiday Contest Announces Week Four Winner: Ashley Mayfield Applegate
item.description: BUSINESS News: Places and Spaces Los Alamos is excited to announce the Week 4 winner of the Local Love Holiday “Snap, Tag, and Share” contest! Congratulations to Ashley Mayfield Applegate, who has won the Week 4 $100 Local Love Gift Card for showing her Local Love at Beef + Leaf Cafe. item.title: Obituary: Leland Stanford Lehman June 16, 1947 – Dec. 11, 2025
item.description: LELAND STANFORD LEHMAN June 16, 1947 – Dec. 11, 2025 Leland Stanford Lehman, 78, of Los Alamos, NM, a proud Army veteran who served in Vietnam, passed away on Thursday, December 11, 2025. Leland “Lelo” served as a rifleman with Company B, 4th Battalion, 47th Infantry Regiment, 9th Infantry Division from July 1967 to June 1969, achieving the rank of Sergeant. item.title: Camp May Road Work Updated Due To Lack Of Snow
item.description: COUNTY News: With high hopes for a snowy ski season at Pajarito Mountain, the Los Alamos Department of Public Utilities (DPU) previously shortened closures on Camp May Road during the holidays. Unfortunately, the mountain is still too dry for skiing, and as such, the road closure schedule is being adjusted again to take advantage of the favorable weather conditions for construction.
